title: Minnesota's 7th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Minnesota's 7th Congressional District will determine who represents the western portion of the state, covering 38 counties from the Canadian border south to Pipestone. Incumbent Republican Michelle Fischbach, first elected in 2020, is seeking a fourth term in a district that is the most conservative in Minnesota — it voted for Donald Trump by 36 points in 2024 and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+18. Four candidates are competing in the August 11 DFL primary: state Rep. Heather Keeler of Moorhead, economic development coordinator Erik Osberg (who won the party endorsement), educator Jared Adams, and Steve Carlson. On the Republican side, Fischbach faces a primary challenge from retired Air Force Major Dave Hughes. The general election is on November 3, 2026, and the Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid Republican.'
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates it 'Solid Republican.'

candidates.name: Michelle Fischbach
candidates.summary: Michelle Fischbach is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2020. She previously served in the Minnesota State Senate from 1996 to 2018, becoming the first woman in state history to serve as President of the Minnesota Senate in 2011, and served as Minnesota's 49th Lieutenant Governor from 2018 to 2019. Fischbach serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the House Rules Committee and has focused on agriculture, Second Amendment rights, and anti-abortion issues.

candidates.name: Dave Hughes
candidates.summary: Dave Hughes is a retired U.S. Air Force Major with 21 years of service and seven combat deployments who is challenging incumbent Michelle Fischbach in the Republican primary. He was the Republican nominee for Minnesota's 7th Congressional District in 2016 and 2018, when he was endorsed by President Donald Trump, and lost both times to then-incumbent Democrat Collin Peterson. Hughes currently works for General Atomics as an MQ-9 UAS (drone) instructor pilot and is a fiscal and social conservative who advocates for term limits, border security, and constitutional freedoms.

candidates.name: Erik Osberg
candidates.summary: Erik Osberg is a first-time candidate for office who won the DFL endorsement for Minnesota's 7th Congressional District in April 2026 with 65% of delegate votes on the first ballot. He has served since 2017 as the Rural Rebound Initiative Coordinator for Otter Tail County, where he co-produced the Emmy Award-winning docuseries 'Rural By Choice.' Osberg previously worked in financial services, started a marketing business, and worked as a sports reporter after earning a degree from Hamline University. He emphasizes rural community development, agriculture, education, and health care access.

candidates.name: Heather Keeler
candidates.summary: Heather Keeler is a Minnesota State Representative serving District 4A (Moorhead area) since 2021 and currently serves as Assistant DFL Floor Leader. She is an enrolled member of the Yankton Sioux Tribe and has been a leading voice on Native American issues including the creation of an office for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Relatives. Prior to elected office, Keeler worked as Assistant Director of Multicultural Recruitment at North Dakota State University and served on Moorhead's Human Rights Commission. She holds a B.S. in Project Management and an M.Ed. in Educational Leadership from Minnesota State University Moorhead.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race. The forecast relies entirely on district fundamentals: Minnesota's 7th is the most conservative district in the state with a Cook PVI of R+18; Donald Trump won it by 36 points in 2024; Cook Political Report rates the race 'Solid Republican.' Incumbent Michelle Fischbach is seeking a fourth term and faces only a primary challenger (Dave Hughes) who has not held elected office. On the Democratic side, a four-candidate DFL primary (August 11) is still unsettled, and none of the candidates have demonstrated the resources or profile to seriously contest a district this Republican-leaning. The structural advantage for Republicans is overwhelming, supporting a safe_r rating. However, the complete absence of any public polling — even internal or partisan surveys — keeps confidence at medium rather than high, as voter sentiment cannot be directly measured.
